Laopu Gold's first-half profit rose 88.18% to 4.267 billion yuan, even as a second, larger revenue figure caused confusion online.

Recognised revenue reached 19.808 billion yuan, up 60.3%. A wider 22.779 billion yuan sales-performance number, up 13.04%, is also circulating — a different measure, not the one behind the profit line. Basic earnings came to 24.16 yuan a share, and the board is paying out 18.02 yuan of it, 74.59% of profit, as an interim dividend.

The read: fixed-price gold jewellery is compounding faster than the metal underneath it.

Gold fell 0.93% to $4,579.50 this morning, and the real story on the board is platinum's held mark finally breaking.

Platinum had carried $1,881 for seven sessions, but that figure sat $19 above Kitco's entire day range — so this desk rewrote the tape to $1,816, a 3.46% correction. Silver eased 0.72% to $68.056. Palladium held an eighth session at $1,336, still inside its own range, so it stayed on the board unchanged.

One metal rewritten, one held, for a stated reason.
